input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 3 columns, and a header row.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

host_fasta.description: Build the host index from this FASTA instead of using a prebuilt one.
host_fasta.help_text: Shared by every dehoster: each builds the index format its own tool needs, so the same reference works whichever one is selected. Mainly for testing — the test profiles build from a small genome rather than depending on hosted index binaries. When set, deacon_db and hostile_db are ignored. Leave unset for real runs.

deacon_db.description: Path to a prebuilt deacon minimizer index file.
deacon_db.help_text: Used when dehoster is deacon. Unlike hostile, deacon's index is a single file, so this is a path to that file rather than a directory plus an index name. The default in the AMDP configs is panhuman-1 (k=31, w=15), the prebuilt index published with deacon. Note that it masks far less than the hostile index does, so the two dehosters do not remove the same reads.

hostile_db.description: Path to the hostile reference database directory. Used when dehoster is hostile or hostess.

hostile_index.description: Name of the hostile reference index to use for dehosting. Default is a masked human reference excluding pathogen regions.

max_reads.description: Cap on reads (single-end) or read pairs (paired-end) retained per sample after dehosting.
max_reads.help_text: Samples above this cap are downsampled to it with fadso (s-leaping reservoir sampling); smaller samples pass through unchanged. Applied after hostile dehosting and gated on hostile's own read counts, so no extra pass over the FASTQs is needed. Leave unset or set to 0 to disable downsampling.

downsample_seed.description: Random seed for read downsampling, fixed for reproducibility.
downsample_seed.help_text: Seed passed to fadso so downsampling is deterministic across runs. Only used when max_reads is set.

hostile_large_input_bytes.description: Total read bytes above which a sample is dehosted by the larger-resourced HOSTILE_CLEAN or HOSTESS copy.
hostile_large_input_bytes.help_text: Hostile's peak memory plateaus rather than tracking input size: samples spanning 15-22 GB of R1 all peaked at the same 43.6 GB, while samples under 100 MB peaked under 5 GB. Samples are therefore routed to one of two resource tiers rather than given a size-scaled allocation. Resources for each tier are set on the _SMALL and _LARGE aliases in the pipeline config. Does not apply to deacon, whose memory is set by the index rather than by the sample, so it runs as a single unrouted process.

dehoster.description: Which host-removal implementation to run, or none to skip host removal.
dehoster.help_text:
deacon is the default. It does not align: it counts how many of each read's minimizers appear in a prebuilt index and drops the read when enough of them do. That makes it substantially faster than the two aligning dehosters, and correspondingly approximate. It keeps no removed reads, so host_bam has no effect under it, and it uses its own reference (panhuman-1 by default), which masks less than the hostile index.

hostess aligns against the host index and keeps what aligns to nothing, reading the alignment stream once instead of duplicating it so it can write the removed reads out as a sorted BAM. Producing the same artefacts it measured 2.4x faster than running hostile twice and realigning.

hostile applies the same method as hostess but cannot produce the removed-read BAM without a second pass.

none skips host removal entirely, reducing the pipeline to optional BAM-to-FASTQ conversion, falco read QC, and multiqc. No host index is required in that case, so every index option is ignored.

host_bam.description: Keep the removed host reads as a coordinate-sorted, indexed BAM.
host_bam.help_text: On by default. Requires dehoster = hostess and has no effect otherwise: hostile discards the host reads and can only recover them with a second alignment pass, and deacon never aligns at all. The BAM loads directly in IGV against the host reference, so an over-aggressive index can be seen rather than inferred from counts. Set false to skip it, along with the samtools flagstat and stats taken over it.

skip_fastp.description: Skip fastp quality control and read trimming.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
